mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stops falling and stabilizes after a sharp drop, weekday discretionary shopping follows with a lag and RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks as commuters return to city-center retail corridors.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -13.3 to -23.6 in t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES stays at or below the current depressed level.

mechanism_narrative: When residential time exceeds its current level by a further step, people substitute local at-home activity for discretionary shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 7 points and stays there for at least 1 week
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 7 points.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases exposure to retail districts during commute chains, so RETAIL_REC turns higher over the next four weeks only when both series improve together.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed near -43 and WORKPLACES dropped to -23.6
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not improve while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise from their current lows over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS visitation signals better weather and higher weekend out-of-home activity, which spills into shopping trips and lifts RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -44.0 to -38.1 in t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week after a PARKS weekly increase of 5 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains near neutral while RETAIL_REC weakens, households are prioritizing essential trips over discretionary outings, and retail demand stays below its previous four-week average over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is around zero to slightly positive
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC moves above its last-four-week mean while GROCERY_PHARM stays near current levels.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained gap where RESIDENTIAL rises and TRANSIT stays deeply negative indicates avoidance of shared spaces, and that pattern suppresses retail visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -40 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 6 for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -43.0 and RESIDENTIAL is 7.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC increases despite TRANSIT remaining below -40 and RESIDENTIAL remaining above 6 for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained pickup in GROCERY_PHARM acts as a short-lag proxy for broader foot traffic and neighborhood activity, producing a modest rebound in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from 0.6 to 1.0 while retail stayed negative
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC stays below its last-four-week average even as GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, the combination of recovering transit access and unchanged workplace attendance reallocates trips from home-based activity toward discretionary spending, so RETAIL_REC rises after a four-week lag.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain heavily depressed while RESIDENTIAL is elevated
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC fails to improve over 28 days after TRANSIT rises without a further collapse in WORKPLACES.
